title: Severance entitlement on termination of employment
description: Determines an employee's severance entitlement when employment ends. Reference logic agreed between the parties (e.g. from a term sheet or HR policy); drafted contract clauses must implement exactly this logic. v2: branching structure with cause subtypes, constructive dismissal, tenure tiers, and redundancy alternatives, plus ontology constraints restricting evaluation to legally possible worlds.

atoms.question: Was the employment terminated by the employer for Cause?
atoms.description: The employer ended the employment for Cause (gross misconduct, persistent underperformance after warnings, or material breach of duties).

atoms.question: Did the Cause consist of gross misconduct?
atoms.description: The Cause relied on was gross misconduct (theft, fraud, violence, or conduct of similar gravity), as opposed to ordinary Cause such as persistent underperformance.

atoms.question: Did the employee resign?
atoms.description: The employment ended by the employee's own resignation.

atoms.question: Was the resignation a constructive dismissal?
atoms.description: The employee resigned in direct response to a fundamental breach of the employment agreement by the employer.

atoms.question: Had the employee completed 12 months of continuous service at the termination date?
atoms.description: At the Termination Date, the employee had at least twelve months of continuous service.

atoms.question: Had the employee completed 5 years of continuous service at the termination date?
atoms.description: At the Termination Date, the employee had at least five years of continuous service.

atoms.question: Was the termination by reason of redundancy?
atoms.description: The role was eliminated or the employer's requirement for the work ceased or diminished.

atoms.question: Was suitable alternative employment offered?
atoms.description: In the redundancy process, the employer offered the employee a suitable alternative role on terms no less favourable overall.

atoms.question: Did the employer give notice of termination in writing?
atoms.description: The employer provided written notice of termination as required by the agreement.

outcomes.label: No severance
outcomes.description: The employee is not entitled to any severance payment.

outcomes.label: Statutory minimum only
outcomes.description: The employee is entitled only to the minimum severance (if any) required by applicable law.

outcomes.label: Standard severance
outcomes.description: One month's base salary per completed year of service.

outcomes.label: Enhanced severance
outcomes.description: Standard severance plus a supplement of three months' base salary.

outcomes.label: Premium redundancy package
outcomes.description: Standard severance plus a supplement of six months' base salary, for long-serving employees made redundant with no suitable alternative role.
